title: NASA Standard for Models and Simulations: Credibility Assessment Scale
authors: Babula, Bertch, Green, Hale, Mosier, Steele, Woods
paraphrase: Scores a simulation on eight factors from 0 to 4 and takes the minimum; the standard leaves the required levels to each project.
notes: Thresholds are project defined, which supports H3 (assumed thresholds). No independence factor beyond technical review and people qualifications.

title: The NASA Standard for Models and Simulations: Deployment Experience
paraphrase: Slides on early adoption of NASA-STD-7009; the scale rates process rigour, is not mandatory, and reviewers found uncertainty statements hard to produce.
notes: Shows credibility scales were contested and optional; relevant to enforceability of admissibility conditions.

title: Assessing Computational Model Credibility Using a Risk-Based Framework: Hemolysis in Centrifugal Blood Pumps
authors: Morrison, Hariharan, Funkhouser, Afshari, Goodin, Horner
paraphrase: Applies ASME V&V 40: required evidence scales with model risk, using physical comparators and uncertainty quantification that grow with risk.
notes: Closest regulatory style precedent for risk scaled credibility. No independence requirement stated in the article.

title: A Credibility Assessment Approach for Scenario-Based Virtual Testing of Automated Driving Functions
paraphrase: Scores credibility of a virtual test bench by comparing simulated behaviour with real test drives replayed as scenarios from measurements.
notes: Validation against physical data and real-measurement replay for automated driving; not robots, not environmental stressors.

title: Virtual Testing of Automated Driving Systems through Credible Simulations
paraphrase: Proposes a risk based credibility framework built on NASA-STD-7009 with lifecycle checks (assumptions, V&V, sensitivity) and acceptance thresholds that vary with how the simulation output is used.
notes: Read via a third party mirror page (arXiv 2609.03760); direct preprint access was rate limited (HTTP 429). Very close to H2 and to the 'what must be shown about the simulator' half of the question. Domain is road vehicles.

title: Validate the Dream Before You Trust Its Verdict: Admissibility for World-Model Simulators
paraphrase: Argues a learned simulator must climb an admissibility ladder (L0 to L4) before its closed loop verdicts count as assurance evidence.
notes: Uses the word admissibility. Abstract does not state rung criteria, independence, real data validation or environmental conditions. Possible scooping risk on terminology.

title: On the Need for a Statistical Foundation in Scenario-Based Testing of Autonomous Vehicles
paraphrase: Introduces a metric checking whether simulated and real test outcomes agree so that simulation based safety claims are statistically defensible.
notes: Directly about how much a safety claim simulated evidence can carry. Road vehicles, not environmental silence.

title: Credibility assessment of a model based on the Robert Bosch Credibility of Simulation Framework
paraphrase: Conference abstract describing an industrial framework that combines VVUQ with risk analysis for a software in the loop braking model.
notes: Criteria and thresholds not visible on the page.

title: Don't believe everything that you see on-screen: How to quantify simulation quality
paraphrase: Conference abstract proposing a correlation process that links vehicle level safety arguments to the credibility of the simulation platform.
notes: Abstract only; no metrics shown.

title: Scaling AI Validation with a Unified Framework for Simulation Trustworthiness
paraphrase: Vendor blog splitting trust into toolchain qualification and fidelity measured against drive logs, and admitting no standard method for realism exists.
notes: Vendor source, not peer reviewed.

title: Predictive Capability Maturity Quantification using Bayesian Network
paraphrase: Turns qualitative simulation maturity ratings into explicit probabilities of adequacy using argumentation and Bayesian networks, with sensitivity checks.
notes: Authors admit weights are assigned by expert judgement. Nuclear domain.

title: Verification and Validation of Simulation Models
paraphrase: Classic review of how to decide model validity; says developer self-validation is common but usually weaker than user involvement or independent third party validation.
notes: Best source found for the independence condition and for the circularity worry (H3).

title: Guidance on the Assurance of Machine Learning in Autonomous Systems (AMLAS)
authors: Hawkins, Paterson, Picardi, Jia, Calinescu, Habli
paraphrase: Safety case patterns and process for ML components; abstract does not mention simulation or environment representativeness.
notes: Full text not read. Do not claim AMLAS says anything on simulation from this retrieval.

title: Guidance on the Safety Assurance of Autonomous Systems in Complex Environments (SACE)
authors: Hawkins, Osborne, Parsons, Nicholson, McDermid, Habli
paraphrase: Safety case patterns for autonomous systems in complex environments; abstract silent on simulation and on ODD detail.
notes: Full text not read.

title: Assessing Confidence with Assurance 2.0
paraphrase: Argues confidence in an assurance case needs positive, negative (defeater) and residual doubt perspectives rather than one number.
notes: Generic framework; no simulation specific conditions in abstract.

title: Defeaters and Eliminative Argumentation in Assurance 2.0
paraphrase: Explains how doubts are recorded as defeaters and resolved by subcases, supporting an eliminative argument.
notes: Natural place to hang simulator admissibility conditions as defeaters.

title: Waymo's Safety Methodologies and Safety Readiness Determinations
authors: Webb, Smith, Ludwick, Victor, Hommes, Favaro, Ivanov, Daniel
paraphrase: Describes simulation as central but validated against road and closed course driving, combined with real driving rather than used alone; notes UL 4600 is non prescriptive.
notes: Replay of real logs treated as more credible than pure synthetic scenarios.

title: Credible Autonomy Safety Argumentation
paraphrase: Lists simulation among several argument styles for autonomy safety; abstract gives no credibility conditions.
notes: Full text not read.

title: 2.7 Using simulation (practical guidance for cobots)
authors: CSI:Cobot, Centre for Assuring Autonomy, University of York
paraphrase: Says a simulation model must be complete and representative for the question, with sensitivity testing, documented limits and operating conditions outside the domain monitored.
notes: Robot specific guidance already listing representativeness and sensitivity conditions; informal, not checkable predicates.

title: Critical Barriers to Assurance and Regulation (C-BARs)
authors: Centre for Assuring Autonomy, University of York
paraphrase: Poses as open problems when simulation alone suffices as evidence and how to bound operating limits.
notes: Frames the question as open, which helps novelty, but does not answer it.

title: Towards Patterns for a Reference Assurance Case for Autonomous Inspection Robots
paraphrase: Proposes reusable assurance patterns combining several verification methods for inspection robots; simulation only listed.
notes: Robot assurance case context only.

title: Generating Certification Evidence for Autonomous Unmanned Aircraft Using Model Checking and Simulation
paraphrase: Proof of concept combining formal verification and flight simulation as certification evidence.
notes: Abstract does not say how simulation credibility is established.

title: JARUS guidelines on SORA, Annex A (system and operation information for a UAS operation)
paraphrase: Asks the applicant to describe and justify performance limits for wind, visibility, temperature and icing, with SITL and HITL listed as validation means.
notes: Supports delegation: applicant states the limits. Annex A is 2017; later SORA versions not read.

title: ISO/TR 23482-1:2020 Robotics, Application of ISO 13482, Part 1: Safety-related test methods
paraphrase: Test methods for personal care robots where the manufacturer chooses the required tests and parameters from a risk assessment.
notes: Best direct evidence for delegation. Full text paywalled, so numeric environmental values not checked.

title: Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 on machinery (EU-OSHA summary page)
paraphrase: Summary says machinery must be safe in intended use or under conditions that can reasonably be foreseen; page gives no environmental values.
notes: Annex III text not read; the summary cannot prove silence on values.

title: EN ISO 12100 and its relation to the Machinery Directive (presentation)
paraphrase: Slides list environmental conditions among machine limits to be considered in risk assessment, without values.
notes: Secondary source for ISO 12100 content.

title: ISO 34503:2023 Road vehicles, Test scenarios for ADS, Specification for operational design domain
paraphrase: Gives a taxonomy for ODD attributes including particulates and illumination while the developer writes the ODD definition.
notes: Taxonomy yes, values no. Road vehicles only.

title: From Safety Standards to Safe Operation with Mobile Robotic Systems Deployment
authors: Belzile, Wanang-Siyapdjie, Karimi, Braga, Iordanova, St-Onge
paraphrase: Finds no standard that is both specific to mobile robots and applicable across deployment scenarios, and validates a risk framework in the field not in simulation.
notes: Supports gap in standards for mobile robots; construction site setting.

title: Modelling of LIDAR sensor disturbances by solid airborne particles
paraphrase: Simulates dust clouds disturbing lidar and compares with lab dust experiments, but only visually with no error metric.
notes: Dust sim to real attempt; no quantitative validation.

title: A Sensor-Aware Phenomenological Framework for Lidar Degradation Simulation and SLAM Robustness Evaluation
paraphrase: Applies synthetic lidar degradations to clean real scans and tests SLAM; not validated against real dust or fog recordings.
notes: Example of synthetic fault injection without physical validation.

title: Instance Performance Difference: A Metric to Measure the Sim-to-Real Gap in Camera Simulation
paraphrase: Proposes a metric of perception performance drop between synthetic and real images, demonstrated on lunar rock detection.
notes: Metric that could serve as a representativeness check; not about dust or glare.

title: S2R-Bench: A Sim-to-Real Evaluation Benchmark for Autonomous Driving
paraphrase: Compares real recorded sensor anomalies with simulated corruptions and finds no simulator matches reality everywhere, with glare among the worst gaps.
notes: Strongest retrieved evidence for H4 on glare; road driving, Beijing, not Gulf.

title: SolarDrive: A High-Contrast Glare Dataset and Diagnostic Probe for Advancing Autonomous Perception
paraphrase: Real glare recordings from Estonia show pedestrian detection collapsing under low sun; full files need an IEEE DataPort subscription.
notes: Not free to download, so unusable under free only rule beyond the abstract.

title: A Survey of Simulators for Autonomous Driving: Taxonomy, Challenges, and Evaluation Metrics
authors: Li, Yuan, Yan, Shen, Wang, Yang
paraphrase: Survey stating simulator outputs differ markedly from real data for adverse weather and that no clear threshold exists for good enough.
notes: Supports that a realism threshold is missing.

title: A Survey on Scenario-Based Testing for Automated Driving Systems in High-Fidelity Simulation
authors: Zhong, Tang, Zhou, de Oliveira Neves, Liu, Ray
paraphrase: Survey of scenario based testing in high fidelity simulators; abstract does not discuss validity.
notes: Included as negative search result.

title: Deep Sequence-to-Sequence Models for GNSS Spoofing Detection
paraphrase: Trains spoofing detectors on a generated synthetic dataset with global random attack scenarios and reports very low error.
notes: Synthetic only per abstract; whether real logs were used is unknown.

title: GNSS Dataset (with Interference and Spoofing), Part I
paraphrase: Real receiver recordings under normal, jammed and spoofed conditions across five constellations.
notes: Free real log source; mid latitude China, not Gulf.

title: Guardian Positioning System (GPS) for Location Based Services
paraphrase: Evaluates detection on real attack traces from Jammertest 2024 and on lab emulated data, reporting both.
notes: Contains both real and synthetic evaluation arms but is not framed as a verdict comparison.

title: MIXED-SENSE: A Mixed Reality Sensor Emulation Framework for Test and Evaluation of UAVs Against False Data Injection Attacks
authors: Pant, Lin, Kim, Sribunma, Goppert, Hwang
paraphrase: Emulates GNSS meaconing against a real PX4 drone and tunes latency and noise to real sensors, but does not compare emulated GNSS to real spoofed receiver output.
notes: Shows the sensor level validation gap.

title: GNSS Interference Complicates Navigation as Hormuz Shipping Disruption Deepens
paraphrase: Trade press report of widespread GNSS jamming and AIS spoofing in the Gulf affecting over 1,100 ships in a day, from third party analytics.
notes: Context that Gulf GNSS interference is real; no logs published in the article.

title: DEWA study assesses PV cleaning robot performance and safety
authors: pv magazine reporting a DEWA study
paraphrase: Field study in Dubai of five cleaning robots found overheating batteries, poor ingress protection and UV damage and proposed a pre deployment checklist; no simulation used.
notes: Only Gulf specific robot reliability evidence found; trade press summary of a Solar Energy paper.

title: Philipp Rosenberger (2023) doctoral thesis, TU Darmstadt (credible simulation, sensor models)
paraphrase: Search result suggests a thesis on credible simulation for automated driving; fetch was blocked so nothing about content was read.
notes: Blocked by bot protection (Anubis). Title not seen. Do not cite.

title: Unreadable paper listing at HAL (IRT SystemX, 2025 conference)
paraphrase: Fetch returned a bot protection page; nothing read.
notes: Blocked. Do not cite.
